name: portfolio-engine
roleLine: An open-source backbone for personal, portfolio, and editorial websites.
shortBio: An Astro theme system that ships routes, layouts, and a typed config surface so you can focus on your content — and is designed to be set up entirely through Claude Code prompts.
summary: portfolio-engine is a layered, first-party (not generic) Astro 6 theme system. Schema, engine-core, editorial-theme, and admin-tools are published as @portfolio-engine/* packages and consumed by your private content repo. Built with Astro 6, Zod 4, Tailwind v4, and pnpm workspaces.
longBio: Most theme systems try to do everything for everyone. portfolio-engine does the opposite — it is built first for a single consumer (its author's own site), then opened up just enough to let other people use it the same way. Being open-source is about transparency, not infinite extensibility.

The engine is split into four strict layers: a pure Zod schema package, an Astro integration (engine-core) that loads config and injects routes, an editorial theme that owns layouts and components, and your consumer site that owns content, config, and overrides. Layers only depend downward. This keeps upgrades boring and breaking changes obvious.

You don't have to copy a template, fight a generator, or read a 60-page README. The recommended setup is to paste docs/downstream/setup-with-claude.md into Claude Code and answer a handful of questions. The agent runs numbered phase scripts that link the engine, write your config, and verify the build. The result is a working site you can deploy to Vercel in minutes.

values.title: First-party, not generic
values.body: Designed for one real consumer at a time. No plugin marketplace, no infinite theme variants, no abstract base classes.

values.title: Explicit override surfaces
values.body: Consumers override named components and styles, not arbitrary files. Override points are declared by the theme and stable across versions.

values.title: Two-repo model
values.body: Engine packages live in a public repo. Your content, config, and identity live in a private repo. They share no git history and no secrets.

values.title: Strict layering
values.body: schema → engine-core → editorial-theme → consumer. Dependencies only point downward. Banned: astro-theme-provider, astro-pages, astro-public.

workingPrinciples.title: Config is JSON, validated by Zod
workingPrinciples.body: site.json, navigation.json, theme.json, features.json — four files, one schema package, friendly errors at build time.

workingPrinciples.title: Content is plain Astro collections
workingPrinciples.body: Profile, projects, writing, testimonials use Astro's native content layer. The engine never touches your markdown.

workingPrinciples.title: Setup runs through Claude Code
workingPrinciples.body: Numbered phase scripts under docs/downstream/scripts let an agent provision your repo with DRY_RUN and SKIP_* flags for safety.

workingPrinciples.title: Three route-ownership modes
workingPrinciples.body: Theme-injected routes, consumer-local routes via a registry JSON, and ordinary src/pages — pick the right mode per page.

workingPrinciples.title: No packaged public/ in the engine
workingPrinciples.body: Engine packages ship code, not assets. Your public/ directory stays yours. CI enforces this rule on every commit.
